answer.evidence: This is a kei van drawn mostly in side profile, so it is not really a box. A large roof band at rows 6-17 (about 12 rows) is lighter yellow at x=32, rows 7-15, and has a highlight. It ends in a darker line at rows 16-17 (L=160), and a dark window and shadow band follows at rows 18-23. Below that the side body spans rows 24-37, with wheels beneath. The roof band is tall enough to read as a roof plane seen from above, not as a 1-2 row rim. The front face is about 20 rows. The roof reading is somewhat ambiguous because the van is mainly a side elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The van has a uniform dark outline around the whole silhouette, wheels and windows. 88% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, against 0-1% for the hedge and cheese stall, so it reads as a near-black sticker line rather than a dark tone of the adjacent material. The yellow body has only about 3-4 steps (base, light, shade, outline) and large smooth panels on the roof, sides and hood with no grain or speckle. Near-flat coverage is 15%, slightly above the cheese stall's 13% and well above the 0% of the hedge and well. It carries 9 visible tones per tile, equal to the hedge but well under the stall (17) and well (20), which are the closest references in structure. Drawing is clean and the forms are readable, but the shading is shallower and the outline is stickerish next to the Beodeul references.
